text:
amy: Quick note — ran a focused probe today to test the "phase-silo" allocator + kernel-probe combo. Saw some interesting KV warmup interactions.

vikram: TL;DR? p99 got worse or better? :thinking: 

amy: p50 ~ same, p95 small win (~6%), but p99 tail increased ~12% on long-context tests. Not huge but actionable.

carmen: did you split prefill vs gen queues fully for this probe or were they still sharing a soft slot?

amy: full siloing — two distinct queue heads, separate token allocators. Prefill bucket uses alloc_target 48, gen uses 24. We also forced kernel selection to prefer matmul_fast for prefill and matmul_low_mem for gen.

ben: can you paste config?

amy: sure:
```yaml
queue_policies:
  prefill:
    alloc_target_tokens: 48
    kernel_hint: matmul_fast
  decode:
    alloc_target_tokens: 24
    kernel_hint: matmul_low_mem
kv:
  priming_window_ms: 1200
  drain_on_handshake: true
```

vikram: logs? sample lines?

amy: snippet from a 2k-context run:
```
[2026-03-15 11:03:22] batch_id=0 stage=prefill formed=10 tokens=480 kernel=matmul_fast latency=20ms
[2026-03-15 11:03:24] batch_id=7 stage=decode formed=3 tokens=72 kernel=matmul_low_mem latency=27ms
[2026-03-15 11:03:29] batch_id=12 stage=prefill formed=1 tokens=48 kernel=matmul_fast kv_hit=false latency=180ms <-- tail kicker
```

ben: that last line looks like KV miss behavior during prefill causing a stall. Did you observe KV contention or eviction storms?

amy: yes — when prefill batches are larger (alloc_target_tokens=48) we occasionally hit cold KV pages for very long sequences; those single-request prefill batches cascade into p99 spikes. decode side looked fine.

carmen: interesting. So siloing reduced interference but amplified cold-KV exposure for large prefill batches. Any kernel fallbacks logged?

amy: matmul_fast had a couple of fallbacks on tensor shapes >4096 where it routed to matmul_generic. Those fallbacks are cheap, but the KV miss + fallback overlapped and magnified latency.

vikram: hypothesis: decrease prefill alloc_target to 32 and increase handshake grace for KV priming (priming_window_ms -> 2000). That should reduce single-large prefill events and give KV a chance to warm.

sarah: +1 to the priming window change. Also consider staggered prefill formation: if prefill queue sees a long-running KV load, allow micro-prefill splitting (emit 2 smaller batches instead of 1).

ben: micro-splitting sounds promising. We had an internal sketch for "prefill_fragment_threshold": if tokens_per_req > X and last_kv_miss_age < Y then split. Do we have telemetry for last_kv_miss_age?

amy: not directly, but latency-bot posted KV miss rate counters this morning. Adding per-request kv_miss_age is cheap in runtime.

latency-bot: KV miss rate (1h): 0.87% overall, prefill-specific miss rate (1h): 1.9%, decode-specific miss rate (1h): 0.2%.

vikram: ok that aligns. Action items: (1) try prefill_alloc_target=32, (2) priming_window_ms=2000, (3) enable prefill_fragment_threshold with conservative defaults (split at >40 tokens into 2 shards), (4) add kv_miss_age counter.

carmen: for kernel selection tweak: instead of forcing matmul_fast for all prefill shapes, allow matmul_selector to check KV priming state. If KV cold and shape large, prefer matmul_low_mem to avoid combined fallback cost. That might reduce p99.

amy: good point. I'll prototype a selector patch: kernel_selector.consider_kv_state(true) and gate matmul_fast behind kv_warm flag.

ben: can we A/B this? run on 10% traffic with the above config and collect p50/p95/p99 + cost delta. Also track avg tokens per batch and KV miss age distribution.

amy: setting up AB now, config in feature-flag "phase_silo_probe_v2". Will push canary at 10%.

vikram: reminder to include per-route dashboards for this flag — we want to see customer breakouts (long-context customers might dominate the tail).

sarah: also ensure rollout has an auto-fallback to baseline if p99 increases by >10% in 15m.

amy: noted. I'll post the PR and data link here when metrics start flowing. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

ben: curious follow-up: if micro-splitting reduces p99 but increases token-count CPU overhead, do we prefer cost or latency? Customer tier gating could route cost-sensitive to original flow. Add that to decision doc.

amy: agree. I'll include a short decision matrix in the PR: latency-first vs cost-first.

vikram: great thread. One more ask — add a short synthetic benchmark that reproduces the KV miss + fallback overlap (2k context, repeated cold-start prefills). If we can reproduce in CI, it's easier to validate.

amy: will do. planning to run the benchmark overnight and post results tomorrow AM.

sarah: thanks — ping when results are in.

amy: ping will land here.
